1 زَرِمَ , (S, K,) aor.
زَرَمَ , (K,) inf. n. زَرَمٌ, (TA,) said of one's urine, (S, K,) and of his flow of tears, and of his speech, (K,) and of his oath, (TA,) and of anything that had gone back, (S,) It became interrupted, or stopped; or it stopped; or ceased; (S, K;) as also ↓ اِزْرَأَمَّ . (K.) And so the former verb said of a sale. (TA.) ―
-b2- And, said of a dog, (S, K,) and of a cat, (K,) His dung, (S, K,) or dry dung, (K,) stopped in his rectum. (S, K.) ＝
-A2- زَرَمَهُ: see 4. ―
-b2- زَرَمَتْ بِهِ She (his mother, S) brought him forth. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
